caption: Diagram 1.5 | Dividing flights Length of flights of stairs For all buildings
description: This is a three-dimensional line diagram of a single flight of stairs, drawn in perspective and viewed from the front-left, with a series of horizontal treads descending towards the right. A dashed curved line, representing a handrail, arcs across the upper part of the flight; at each end it meets a vertical dashed line that drops down to the lower treads, marking the division of the flight into two sections. Above the stairs, a horizontal dimension line with arrowheads at each end runs from the left-hand edge of the flight to the dividing handrail, accompanied by the text "If more than 2m wide the flight should be divided". In the top-left corner the text reads "See para 1.15". At the bottom right, a shorter horizontal dimension line with arrowheads runs from the dividing handrail to the right-hand edge of the flight, marking the width of one section. Below the stairs, the text states "Divisions of flights should not be more than 2m wide, measured between the inside edges of handrails". A green band along the bottom edge carries the white text "Diagram 1.5 Dividing flights".
